checks.result: The complete focused Windows supervision report remained ok=true and added delayedReadinessCleanup=true. The fixture starts an immediate descendant, marks an in-flight compatible readiness response, delays that response, and ignores graceful shutdown. Stop during that window returned only after both root and descendant were already dead; the start worker returned Stopped and Retry was enabled only after cleanup.
Architecture, backlog invariants, and generated planning views passed. The incremental production change is confined to the supervisor plus its two native fixtures.

evidence: Startup rechecks the active attempt after a compatible readiness response and before returning success.

Every post-spawn startup failure now terminates and waits for the contained process tree before launch returns; a late successful launch that loses publication ownership likewise keeps launching true until private cleanup completes.
A waiting stop cannot clear stopping, return a retryable snapshot, or permit a new start until the prior root and immediate descendant are dead.
The committed delayed-compatible-readiness fixture deterministically covers the exact reviewer reproduction and asserts process liveness immediately when stop returns.
The earlier real-sidecar, async cancellation, containment, failure-classification, diagnostics, crash/retry, and restart-limit matrix remains in the same focused passing executable.
No renderer, Python service, contract, dependency, UI reference, or build behavior changed, so broader profiles remain correctly deferred to S03 integration review.
The seven-file range contains the three-file focused production/test delta plus immutable prior evidence and task review/generated-view records.
The governing ADR and documentation from the superseded remediation remain accurate: lifecycle completion is serialized through complete process-tree termination.
No scope expansion or unresolved verification item remains.
